title: Dexa API
description: Run many decider and extractor tasks in one compact, non-streaming request. Official SDKs for TypeScript, Python, Ruby, Rust, Java and .NET.
text: The Dexa API runs many small judgement tasks against the same context in a single request. Instead of paying for one completion per question, you send a list of tasks and get back every answer in one response. json { "model" : "decider-extractor-v1" , "context" : "User says: renew subscription for 2 years. Previous plan expired 3 months ago." , "tasks" : [ { "type" : "decide" , "name" : "should_renew" , "question" : "Should we offer a renewal discount?" , "options" : [ "yes" , "no" ] } , { "type" : "extract" , "name" : "renew_term" , "instruction" : "Extract the renewal term in months" , "keys" : [ "months" ] } ] } json { "id" : "req_9X2kFvTnQpR4w" , "model" : "decider-extractor-v1" , "results" : { "should_renew" : { "value" : "yes" } , "renew_term" : { "months" : 24 } } , "usage" : { "prompt_tokens" : 61 , "completion_tokens" : 9 , "total_tokens" : 70 } } What it is built for # One call, many answers. Ten questions about one document cost one round trip, not ten. Tiny outputs. Decisions are short strings, extractions are small objects. Pure decisions are designed to stay under ten completion tokens. Deterministic by default. temperature defaults to 0 . OpenAI-shaped. model , messages , choices , usage mean existing OpenAI tooling and mental models carry over. Note The API is non-streaming by design. There is no SSE endpoint and none is planned for the current version. Start here # Installation - add an SDK to your project Quickstart - first request in five minutes Authentication - tokens and base URLs Task types - deciders and extractors in depth API reference - every endpoint and field Endpoints # Endpoint Use it for POST /v1/tasks Any mix of decider and extractor tasks POST /v1/decide-extract Backwards-compatible alias of /v1/tasks POST /decide A single decider task, without wrapping it in a list POST /extract A single extractor task, without wrapping it in a list Prefer /v1/tasks . The other three exist so that simple calls stay simple and so that clients written against the first version of the contract keep working. Client libraries # Language Package Client class TypeScript @dsainvg/dexa-ai-sdk DexaAiSdkClient Python dexa-ai-sdk DexaAiSdk Ruby gem DexaAiSdk Rust dexa-ai-sdk crate DexaAiSdk Java Maven artifact DexaAiSdk .NET DexaAiSdk package DexaAiSdkClient C++ has no generated client. Call the HTTP API directly from any HTTP library, the payloads are plain JSON. See clients for a worked C++ example.

title: Installation
description: Add the TypeScript, Python, Ruby, Rust, Java or .NET client to your project.
text: Every client is generated from the same OpenAPI contract, so they all expose the same operations with the same field names. Pick the one that matches your stack. Note TypeScript and Python install from npm and PyPI. Ruby, Rust, Java and .NET are published as downloadable files on the GitHub Release, so you fetch them by URL. The installation commands below assume the package names Fern generates; check the real ones in packages/sdk-<language>/ after your first generation, or in the publishing notes . TypeScript # bash npm install @dsainvg/dexa-ai-sdk bash pnpm add @dsainvg/dexa-ai-sdk # or yarn add @dsainvg/dexa-ai-sdk Requires Node 18 or newer. Ships type declarations, no any in sight. ts import { DexaAiSdkClient } from "@dsainvg/dexa-ai-sdk" ; const client = new DexaAiSdkClient ({ baseUrl : "http://localhost:8080" , token : process. env . DEXA_TOKEN , }); Python # bash pip install dexa-ai-sdk bash uv add dexa-ai-sdk Requires Python 3.9 or newer. An async client is available alongside the synchronous one. python from dexa_ai_sdk import DexaAiSdk client = DexaAiSdk( base_url= "http://localhost:8080" , token= "..." , ) Ruby # bash gem install decide_extractor ruby require "decide_extractor" client = DexaAiSdk .new( base_url: "http://localhost:8080" , token: ENV .fetch( "DEXA_TOKEN" ) ) Rust # toml # Cargo.toml [dependencies] dexa-ai-sdk = "0.3" rust use dexa-ai-sdk::DexaAiSdk; let client = DexaAiSdk:: builder () . base_url ( "http://localhost:8080" ) . build ()?; Java # Maven coordinates are com.dsainvg:dexa-ai-sdk . The SDK is not on Maven Central, so install the jar from the release: bash curl -L -o dexa-ai-sdk.jar \ https://github.com/dsainvg/decide-extract-sdk/releases/download/v0.5.0/java-dexa-ai-sdk-0.5.0.jar mvn install:install-file -Dfile=dexa-ai-sdk.jar -DgroupId=com.dsainvg -DartifactId=dexa-ai-sdk -Dversion=0.5.0 xml < dependency > < groupId > com.dsainvg </ groupId > < artifactId > dexa-ai-sdk </ artifactId > < version > 0.5.0 </ version > </ dependency > java var client = DexaAiSdkClient.builder() .baseUrl( "http://localhost:8080" ) .token(System.getenv( "DEXA_TOKEN" )) .build(); .NET # bash dotnet add package DexaAiSdk csharp using DexaAiSdk; var client = new DexaAiSdkClient( new DexaAiSdkClientOptions { BaseUrl = "http://localhost:8080" , Token = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable( "DEXA_TOKEN" ), }); C++ # There is no generated C++ client. The API is plain JSON over HTTP, so any HTTP library works. See clients for a complete example using curl and nlohmann/json . Working against the sources instead # To use a client before it is published, generate it locally: bash git clone https://github.com/dsainvg/decide-extract-sdk.git cd dexa-ai-sdk npm install npm run fern:generate # requires Docker Then reference the package from packages/sdk-ts or packages/sdk-py directly. Repository layout explains the rest.

title: Quickstart
description: Send your first request with the HTTP API and with each client library.
text: This walks through one request end to end: decide whether to renew, and extract the renewal term, in a single call. With curl # The API is plain HTTP and JSON, so anything that can POST works. bash curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/tasks \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEXA_TOKEN " \ -d '{ "model": "decider-extractor-v1", "context": "User says: renew subscription for 2 years. Previous plan expired 3 months ago.", "tasks": [ { "type": "decide", "name": "should_renew", "question": "Should we offer a renewal discount?", "options": ["yes", "no"] }, { "type": "extract", "name": "renew_term", "instruction": "Extract the renewal term in months", "keys": ["months"] } ] }' json { "id" : "req_9X2kFvTnQpR4w" , "model" : "decider-extractor-v1" , "choices" : [ { "message" : { "role" : "assistant" , "content" : "{\"should_renew\":{\"value\":\"yes\"},\"renew_term\":{\"months\":24}}" } , "finish_reason" : "stop" } ] , "results" : { "should_renew" : { "value" : "yes" } , "renew_term" : { "months" : 24 } } , "usage" : { "prompt_tokens" : 61 , "completion_tokens" : 9 , "total_tokens" : 70 } } Read the answers from results , keyed by each task's name . choices[0].message.content carries the same data as a JSON string, for OpenAI-shaped clients. TypeScript # ts import { DexaAiSdkClient } from "@dsainvg/dexa-ai-sdk" ; const client = new DexaAiSdkClient ({ baseUrl : "http://localhost:8080" , token : process. env . DEXA_TOKEN , }); const response = await client. tasks . decideExtract ({ model : "decider-extractor-v1" , context : "User says: renew subscription for 2 years. Previous plan expired 3 months ago." , tasks : [ { type : "decide" , name : "should_renew" , question : "Should we offer a renewal discount?" , options : [ "yes" , "no" ], }, { type : "extract" , name : "renew_term" , instruction : "Extract the renewal term in months" , keys : [ "months" ], }, ], }); console . log (response. results ?. should_renew ); Python # python import os from dexa_ai_sdk import DexaAiSdk client = DexaAiSdk( base_url= "http://localhost:8080" , token=os.environ[ "DEXA_TOKEN" ], ) response = client.tasks.decide_extract( model= "decider-extractor-v1" , context= "User says: renew subscription for 2 years. Previous plan expired 3 months ago." , tasks=[ { "type" : "decide" , "name" : "should_renew" , "question" : "Should we offer a renewal discount?" , "options" : [ "yes" , "no" ], }, { "type" : "extract" , "name" : "renew_term" , "instruction" : "Extract the renewal term in months" , "keys" : [ "months" ], }, ], ) print (response.results) Ruby # ruby response = client.tasks.decide_extract( model: "decider-extractor-v1" , context: "User says: renew subscription for 2 years. Previous plan expired 3 months ago." , tasks: [ { type: "decide" , name: "should_renew" , question: "Should we offer a renewal discount?" , options: [ "yes" , "no" ] }, { type: "extract" , name: "renew_term" , instruction: "Extract the renewal term in months" , keys: [ "months" ] } ] ) puts response.resu

title: Authentication
description: How tokens are sent, where they come from, and what happens when one is missing.
text: Bearer tokens # Every request authenticates with an API key in the standard OpenAI-style header: http POST /v1/tasks HTTP/1.1 Host : api.example.com Authorization : Bearer sk-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx Content-Type : application/json In the clients # Each generated client takes the token once, at construction, instead of on every call. ts const client = new DexaAiSdkClient ({ baseUrl, token }); python client = DexaAiSdk(base_url=base_url, token=token) ruby client = DexaAiSdk .new( base_url: base_url, token: token) rust let client = DexaAiSdk:: builder (). token (token). build ()?; java var client = DexaAiSdkClient.builder().token(token).build(); csharp var client = new DexaAiSdkClient( new DexaAiSdkClientOptions { Token = token }); Keep the token in an environment variable or your platform's secret store. Never commit it, and never put it in a URL, since URLs end up in logs. bash export DEXA_TOKEN= "sk-..." Failures # A missing or invalid key is rejected before any model runs, so a bad key costs nothing. Status Meaning What to do 401 No key, or the key is not recognised Check Authorization is present and well-formed 403 Key is valid but not allowed to use this model Use a model the key has access to json { "error" : { "type" : "authentication_error" , "message" : "Invalid API key provided" , "code" : "invalid_api_key" } } The body always has the same shape, whatever went wrong. See errors .

title: Configuration
description: Base URLs, model selection, determinism and the controls every request shares.
text: Every endpoint, single or batched, accepts the same generation controls. Field Type Default Notes model string required Which model runs the tasks context string - Free-form text the tasks read. Required unless messages is given messages array - OpenAI-style turns. Required unless context is given temperature number 0 0 to 2 . 0 is deterministic max_output_tokens integer 16 1 to 4096 . Raise it when extracting many fields response_format object { "type": "json_object" } JSON output is enforced target_language enum - Language for the results output_language enum - Alias of target_language Base URL # The contract's default server is http://localhost:8080 . Point clients at your deployment: ts new DexaAiSdkClient ({ baseUrl : "https://api.example.com" }); python DexaAiSdk(base_url= "https://api.example.com" , token=token) Determinism # temperature defaults to 0 , which makes repeated calls against the same input produce the same answer. That is what you want for routing and compliance decisions. If you need variation, raise it deliberately: json { "temperature" : 0.7 } Decisions are short by design. If a decide task comes back truncated, the whole request hit max_output_tokens , not that one task. The default of 16 is plenty for several decisions; raise it when a batch contains an extractor pulling a larger object. JSON output # response_format only accepts json_object , which is also the default, so you can leave it out. It exists so the request shape matches the OpenAI API and so it can be relaxed later without breaking clients. Language of the results # target_language (or its alias output_language ) asks for the values in results to come back in a given language. Supported values: en , es , fr , de , it , pt , nl , ru , ja , ko , zh , ar , hi , tr , pl , sv , da , no , fi , cs A task can override the request default: json { "target_language" : "en" , "tasks" : [ { "type" : "decide" , "name" : "intent" , "question" : "What is the customer asking for?" , "target_language" : "fr" } ] } Tip Keep the keys stable and only translate the values. Downstream code that reads results.invoice_number keeps working when the content language changes.

title: Task types
description: How decider and extractor tasks are shaped, named, and answered.
text: Every task is one entry in the tasks array and is one of two kinds, chosen by its type field. The field is the discriminator: the API routes on it, and the generated clients type it as a union of DecideTask and ExtractTask . Decider # A decider answers one question with one value selected from a set of choices. json { "type" : "decide" , "name" : "should_renew" , "question" : "Should we offer a renewal discount?" , "options" : [ "yes" , "no" ] } Field Required Notes type yes Always decide name yes Key this result appears under in results . Has no effect on LLM inference. question yes The question to answer options no Allowed answers. Defaults to ["yes", "no"] for boolean decisions; may have more than 2 options. choices no Alias of options . Defaults to ["yes", "no"] instruction no Extra guidance for this one decision target_language no Overrides the request language for this task id no Legacy alias of name Boolean Decisions and Multi-Option Decisions # By default, omitting options (or choices ) creates a boolean decision defaulting to ["yes", "no"] . When needed, deciders can specify more than two options (for example, ["approve", "reject", "escalate"] ). Decision Probabilities and "Not Sure" # Every decision returns a probabilities map providing the estimated likelihood for each option: json { "should_renew" : { "value" : "yes" , "probabilities" : { "yes" : 0.85 , "no" : 0.10 } , "reason" : "Two-year term and a three-month lapse" } } Note The option probabilities may not add up to 1.0 . In such cases, the remaining probability ( 1.0 - sum(probabilities) ) should be treated as the model's probability of being not sure / uncertain. reason costs completion tokens. Leave it out of the request if you do not read it, and lower max_output_tokens accordingly. Extractor # An extractor answers an extraction question against the context. There are no keys or fields : the question itself specifies what to extract (a single extraction per task, rather than multiple fields). json { "type" : "extract" , "name" : "renew_term" , "question" : "What is the renewal term?" } Field Required Notes type yes Always extract name yes Key this result appears under in results . Has no effect on LLM inference. question yes The extraction question or prompt (previously instruction ) instruction no Backward-compatible alias for question schema no Optional JSON-Schema-like object describing shape target_language no Overrides the request language for this task id no Legacy alias of name Answered as: json { "renew_term" : { "value" : "24 months" } } Naming # name is the key in results , so choose names your code can read out loud: json { "name" : "should_renew" } json { "results" : { "should_renew" : { "value" : "yes" , "probabilities" : { "yes" : 0.85 , "no" : 0.10 } } } } The pattern is [a-zA-Z0-9_][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]{0,63} : letters, digits, underscore, dot and hyphen, up to 64 characters, and it cannot start with a dot or a hyphen. Names must be unique within a request; duplicates overwrite each other in results . Important The name field has no effect on LLM inference . It is strictly used as the dictionary key to index and return each task's answer in results . Warning Naming a field id used to be the only way. It still works, but name is canonical. Pick one and stay with it, or results will be keyed by whichever the model preferred. Deciders and extractors together # Tasks of both kinds go in one array and are answered together, in one call: json { "model" : "decider-extractor-v1" , "

title: Documentation versions
description: Every release keeps its own copy of the docs, and the root always shows the newest.
text: The documentation is versioned. Each release is published under its own path and is never rewritten afterwards, so a link to the docs that shipped with a given version keeps showing that version. Path What it is / the newest published version /v0-5-0/ the docs exactly as they shipped with 0.5.0 /v0-3-5/ the docs exactly as they shipped with 0.3.5 A version turns into a path by replacing the dots with dashes, so 0.3.5 is v0-3-5 . There is no redirect between them on purpose: a reader who followed a versioned link stays on the version they asked for. Use the selector in the header to move between versions. It reads versions.json , which lists every published version with the newest first. What gets published when # On every push to main , the docs are built and the Docs workflow publishes them: The site for the current contract version is written to /vX-Y-Z/ . The root is refreshed with the same build. No other version folder is touched. versions.json is rewritten to match. Two consequences follow from that. Rebuilding the same version replaces that one folder and leaves the history intact, and a new version adds a folder rather than overwriting the one before it. Running it locally # bash npm run docs:build # build into sites/ npm run docs:serve # serve it on http://localhost:4321 npm run docs:publish pushes the build to the sites branch. It only ever writes that one branch, and only that one version folder. See also # Publishing for what goes to which registry. Deploying the docs for how the site is served.

title: Single tasks
description: The /decide and /extract shortcuts for when there is exactly one task.
text: Batching exists to share context across tasks. When you only have one task, POST /decide and POST /extract skip the array and give you a flatter request and response. POST /decide # bash curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/decide \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEXA_TOKEN " \ -d '{ "model": "decider-extractor-v1", "context": "User says: renew subscription for 2 years. Previous plan expired 3 months ago.", "question": "Should we offer a renewal discount?", "options": ["yes", "no"] }' json { "id" : "req_4Kd8PwPq" , "model" : "decider-extractor-v1" , "choices" : [ { "message" : { "role" : "assistant" , "content" : "{\"value\":\"yes\"}" } , "finish_reason" : "stop" } ] , "result" : { "value" : "yes" , "probabilities" : { "yes" : 0.85 , "no" : 0.10 } , "reason" : "Two-year term and a three-month lapse" } , "decision" : { "value" : "yes" , "probabilities" : { "yes" : 0.85 , "no" : 0.10 } , "reason" : "Two-year term and a three-month lapse" } , "value" : "yes" , "usage" : { "prompt_tokens" : 44 , "completion_tokens" : 6 , "total_tokens" : 50 } } Field Required Notes model yes Model identifier question yes The question to answer context / messages yes One of the two, same rule as /v1/tasks options / choices no Allowed answers. Defaults to ["yes", "no"] for boolean decisions; can specify more than 2 options instruction no Extra guidance temperature , max_output_tokens , response_format no Same as everywhere The response carries the answer three times on purpose: result is canonical, decision is an alias for OpenAI-shaped clients that expect a decision field, and value is the bare string for callers that only want the answer. In result , probabilities maps each option to its estimated likelihood. If probabilities do not add up to 1.0, the remaining probability is treated as the model being not sure / uncertain. POST /extract # bash curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/extract \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEXA_TOKEN " \ -d '{ "model": "decider-extractor-v1", "context": "User says: renew subscription for 2 years. Previous plan expired 3 months ago.", "question": "What is the renewal term?" }' json { "id" : "req_7Lq2XzVb" , "model" : "decider-extractor-v1" , "choices" : [ { "message" : { "role" : "assistant" , "content" : "24 months" } , "finish_reason" : "stop" } ] , "result" : { "value" : "24 months" } , "data" : { "value" : "24 months" } , "value" : "24 months" , "usage" : { "prompt_tokens" : 41 , "completion_tokens" : 5 , "total_tokens" : 46 } } result is canonical, data is the alias, and value gives the extracted string directly. There are no keys or fields : question is required (with instruction accepted as an alias) and extracts a single target value. Which one should I use # Situation Use One task, ever /decide or /extract Several tasks over the same context /v1/tasks A task list that sometimes has one item /v1/tasks anyway, so the code has one path Tip /v1/tasks is a strict superset. If your code can handle a list, it can handle everything, and you avoid two code paths for the same call.

title: Multimodal input
description: Attaching images and audio to a request through messages content parts.
text: Tasks can read images and audio as well as text. Inputs are attached at the request level with images and audio , or inside a message as content parts. Both forms reach the same model context. Images # json { "model" : "decider-extractor-v1" , "context" : "Which of these two invoices is larger?" , "images" : [ { "type" : "url" , "url" : "https://example.com/invoice-a.png" } , { "type" : "base64" , "data" : "iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUg..." , "mime_type" : "image/png" } ] , "tasks" : [ { "type" : "decide" , "name" : "a_is_larger" , "question" : "Is invoice A larger than invoice B?" , "options" : [ "yes" , "no" ] } , { "type" : "extract" , "name" : "invoice_a_total" , "instruction" : "Extract the total from invoice A" , "keys" : [ "amount" , "currency" ] } ] } Field Notes type url or base64 url Set when type is url data Base64-encoded payload, set when type is base64 mime_type image/png , image/jpeg , image/webp , image/gif Always send mime_type with base64 data. Without it the server has to guess the format from the first bytes, which is slower and occasionally wrong. Audio # json { "model" : "decider-extractor-v1" , "context" : "Summarise what the customer asked for" , "audio" : [ { "type" : "base64" , "data" : "SUQzBAAAAA..." , "mime_type" : "audio/mp3" } ] , "tasks" : [ { "type" : "extract" , "name" : "requested_items" , "instruction" : "Extract the items the customer asked about" , "keys" : [ "items" ] } ] } Field Notes type url or base64 url Set when type is url data Base64-encoded payload, set when type is base64 mime_type audio/mp3 , audio/wav , audio/mpeg , audio/ogg , audio/mp4 Content parts in messages # When you want per-turn control, use messages instead of context . content is either a plain string or a list of parts: json { "model" : "decider-extractor-v1" , "messages" : [ { "role" : "system" , "content" : "You are extracting from support calls." } , { "role" : "user" , "content" : [ { "type" : "text" , "text" : "Which document is this, and what is the total?" } , { "type" : "image_url" , "image_url" : { "url" : "https://example.com/doc.png" , "detail" : "high" } } ] } ] , "tasks" : [ { "type" : "extract" , "name" : "document" , "instruction" : "Extract the document type and total" , "keys" : [ "type" , "total" ] } ] } Content part fields # Field Notes type text , image_url , image , audio , input_audio text Set when type is text language Language of this part, for example en or ja image_url { "url": "...", "detail": "low" | "high" | "auto" } image An ImageInput object audio , input_audio An AudioInput object image_url is the OpenAI-compatible spelling and takes a URL plus a detail hint. image is the same object used by the top-level images array, which is more convenient when the bytes are already base64. audio and input_audio are aliases, so existing OpenAI code can be moved over unchanged. Message fields # Field Required Notes role yes system , user or assistant content yes String, or a list of content parts language no Language of the whole message Choosing between them # Situation Use Plain text, no system prompt context N

title: Structured output
description: How results are shaped, keyed, and repeated for OpenAI compatibility.
text: results # The canonical answer is results , an object keyed by each task's name : json { "results" : { "should_renew" : { "value" : "yes" } , "renew_term" : { "months" : 24 } } } It is a free-form object, so decider answers are { value, reason? } objects and extractor answers are whatever the task asked for. Generated clients type the known paths and let you index the rest. Tip Iterate over the keys you sent rather than the keys you got back. A model asked for should_renew will return should_renew , but do not let a missing key crash the caller. tasks, the alias # tasks carries the same object as results , kept for clients written against the first version of the contract. Exactly one of the two is populated in practice; read results unless you are maintaining an old client. choices # The OpenAI-shaped part of the response: json { "choices" : [ { "message" : { "role" : "assistant" , "content" : "{\"should_renew\":{\"value\":\"yes\"},\"renew_term\":{\"months\":24}}" } , "finish_reason" : "stop" } ] } content is the whole results object encoded as a JSON string. You never need it if you read results , but it is what makes the response usable by generic OpenAI tooling. finish_reason is one of: Value Meaning stop Finished normally. The normal case length Hit max_output_tokens before finishing reason : content_filter Stopped by a safety filter length on a batch means at least one task was truncated, usually an extractor that wanted more room. Raise max_output_tokens and retry. content_filter is not retryable with the same input; change the context. usage # json { "usage" : { "prompt_tokens" : 61 , "completion_tokens" : 9 , "total_tokens" : 70 } } All three are always present and never negative. total_tokens is prompt_tokens + completion_tokens . What a batch costs # Everything is billed on one prompt that contains the context, the images, the audio and every task, plus one completion holding every answer. Tasks Context prompt_tokens (approx.) 1 decide one sentence ~40 5 mixed tasks one paragraph ~90 10 mixed tasks + image a page and a screenshot ~1200 One request with ten tasks costs a little more than a single call, and far less than ten. That trade is the point of the API.

title: Errors
description: Status codes, the error body, and what to do about each failure.
text: Error body # Every failure, at every endpoint, returns the same shape: json { "error" : { "type" : "invalid_request_error" , "message" : "tasks must contain at least one task" , "param" : "tasks" , "code" : "too_few_tasks" } } Field Always present Notes type yes Broad category, invalid_request_error style message yes Human-readable, safe to log param no Which field was wrong code no Stable machine-readable code, safe to branch on Branch on code , log message , show neither to end users. Status codes # Status When it happens Retry? 400 Malformed JSON, unknown field, missing context or messages No, fix the request 401 Missing or invalid API key No 403 Key cannot use this model No 422 Well-formed JSON, invalid values No, fix the request 429 Rate limited Yes, after Retry-After 500 Server-side failure Yes, with backoff Common errors # 400 no input # json { "error" : { "type" : "invalid_request_error" , "message" : "one of context or messages is required" , "code" : "missing_input" } } Every endpoint needs text to work from. Send context for a single blob, or messages when you need roles or content parts. 400 unknown field # json { "error" : { "type" : "invalid_request_error" , "message" : "Unrecognized property: 'stream'" , "param" : "stream" , "code" : "unknown_field" } } Requests are strict. Unknown fields are rejected rather than ignored, so a typo fails loudly instead of silently doing nothing. The API is also non-streaming, so stream is never valid. 422 bad task name # json { "error" : { "type" : "validation_error" , "message" : "name must match ^[a-zA-Z0-9_][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]{0,63}$" , "param" : "tasks[1].name" , "code" : "invalid_task_name" } } param points at the exact index in tasks that failed. 422 out of range # json { "error" : { "type" : "validation_error" , "message" : "max_output_tokens must be between 1 and 4096" , "param" : "max_output_tokens" , "code" : "out_of_range" } } temperature is 0 to 2 , max_output_tokens is 1 to 4096 . 429 rate limited # json { "error" : { "type" : "rate_limit_error" , "message" : "Rate limit reached" , "code" : "rate_limit_exceeded" } } Honour the Retry-After header, fall back to exponential backoff with jitter, and batch more tasks per call rather than retrying in a tight loop. 500 server error # json { "error" : { "type" : "api_error" , "message" : "Internal server error" , "code" : "internal_error" } } Retry with backoff. If it persists, the request id from the response is what support needs. Handling in the clients # The generated clients throw on any non-2xx response, with the status code and the parsed error body attached. ts import { DexaAiSdkError } from "@dsainvg/dexa-ai-sdk" ; try { await client. tasks . decideExtract (request); } catch (error) { if (error instanceof DexaAiSdkError ) { console . error (error. statusCode , error. body ?. error ?. code ); } } python from dexa_ai_sdk.core.api_error import ApiError try : client.tasks.decide_extract(request) except ApiError as error: print (error.status_code, error.body[ "error" ][ "code" ]) Retry only on 429 and 5xx . Everything else needs a change to the request.

title: Versioning and migration
description: How versions are numbered, what changed between them, and how to upgrade.
text: One version, everything # The version lives in exactly one place, info.version in the OpenAPI contract. It is stamped into every generated client and into both registries, so 0.5.0 on npm, on PyPI, in the Git tag and in the response envelope are always the same number. Version Released What changed 0.5.0 current /v1/tasks , multimodal input, language selection, DecideResult 0.2.0 yes Single /v1/decide-extract endpoint 0.1.0 yes First contract, POST /v1/decide-extract What changed in 0.5.0 # Renamed, with aliases. Task.id became Task.name , and results was added as the canonical response field next to tasks . Both old names still work. Before Now Status tasks[].id tasks[].name id still accepted response.tasks response.results tasks still returned DecideTask.options DecideTask.options choices added as an alias ExtractTask.keys ExtractTask.keys fields added as an alias POST /v1/decide-extract POST /v1/tasks old path still serves Added POST /v1/tasks , POST /decide , POST /extract images , audio , and content parts on messages target_language / output_language DecideResult with an optional reason result , decision and value on the decide response Removed: nothing. No field or endpoint in 0.2.0 was taken away. Migrating from 0.2.0 # Upgrade the client package. Rename id to name in your task builders, if you can. id still works, so this is optional today and worth doing before it is removed. Prefer results over tasks when reading responses. Move the endpoint to /v1/tasks when convenient. diff -const response = await client.tasks.decideExtract({ +const response = await client.tasks.runTasks({ model, context, tasks: [ - { type: "decide", id: "should_renew", question, options: ["yes", "no"] }, + { type: "decide", name: "should_renew", question, options: ["yes", "no"] }, ], }); -response.tasks?.should_renew; +response.results?.should_renew; Pinning # Pin exactly in production. Clients are generated, and a patch release can rename a symbol when the contract gains a field. bash npm install @dsainvg/dexa-ai-sdk@0.5.0 pip install dexa-ai-sdk==0.5.0 Take a minor version to get new fields and endpoints, a patch for fixes only, and expect a major version to change something you depend on. Breaking changes # A breaking change is anything that can make a correct program wrong: removing a field, renaming one, changing a type, changing a default, tightening validation. Those land in a major version, ship with a note in CHANGELOG.md , and keep the old behaviour for at least one minor release. Non-breaking additions, new optional fields, new enum values and new endpoints ship in a minor version. When new enum values appear, ignore values you do not recognise rather than failing.

title: Troubleshooting
description: Symptoms, causes and fixes for the problems that actually come up.
headings: 400: one of context or messages is required#
422: tasks must contain at least one task#
Answers come back in the wrong language#
Everything is slow and the bill went up#
The client cannot reach the server#
Generated client names differ from the docs#
text: 400: one of context or messages is required # Every endpoint needs something to work from. Send context as a single string, or messages when you need roles or content parts. The two are alternatives, never both. 400: Unrecognized property # Requests are strict. The most common offenders are stream (this API never streams) and snake_case fields that do not exist, such as max_tokens instead of max_output_tokens . The error names the offending property. 400: Unrecognized property: 'max_tokens' # The field is max_output_tokens , matching OpenAI's newer naming rather than the old one. 422: tasks must contain at least one task # tasks cannot be empty. If you built the list dynamically and it came out empty, check the filter that filled it before calling. 422: task names must be unique # Two tasks shared a name , so one answer overwrote the other in results . This passes validation and produces wrong data, so validate names yourself when you build task lists dynamically. The answer is cut off # finish_reason is length . The batch hit max_output_tokens , usually an extractor asking for more fields than the default 16 tokens allows. Raise it, or split the batch. json { "max_output_tokens" : 256 } finish_reason is content_filter # The request was stopped by a safety filter. Retrying the same input gives the same result; change the content or split the request. Answers come back in the wrong language # Set target_language , or output_language if that reads better. It applies to the whole request, and each task can override it. json { "target_language" : "fr" } Keep keys in English and translate values. Code that reads results.invoice_number keeps working when the language changes. 401 on every call # Check the header is Authorization: Bearer <token> and not Authorization: <token> , and that the token is not quoted, has no trailing newline from a .env file, and has not been rotated out from under the process. Everything is slow and the bill went up # Look at usage.prompt_tokens . Batching many tasks over a large context, or attaching base64 media, dominates the cost. Put more tasks in each call instead of making more calls, and trim the context to what the tasks actually need. Base64 media is rejected # Send mime_type . The server should not have to infer the format from the payload's first bytes, and some clients require it. Valid values are image/png , image/jpeg , image/webp , image/gif , audio/mp3 , audio/wav , audio/mpeg , audio/ogg , audio/mp4 . The client cannot reach the server # The contract's default base URL is http://localhost:8080 . Against anything else, set baseUrl (or base_url in Python, base_url in Ruby) explicitly. Generated client names differ from the docs # Method names follow the contract's operation ids and tag names, so a rename in fern/openapi/openapi.yml changes them after the next generation. Check the generated source in packages/sdk-<language>/ if something does not match, and upgrade your client.

title: API overview
description: Endpoints, conventions and shared request fields.
text: Base URL in development: http://localhost:8080 . All endpoints are POST , take and return application/json , and authenticate with Authorization: Bearer <token> . Endpoints # Endpoint Operation id Request Response /v1/tasks runTasks RunTasksRequest RunTasksResponse /v1/decide-extract decideExtract RunTasksRequest RunTasksResponse /decide decide DecideRequest DecideResponse /extract extract ExtractRequest ExtractResponse POST /v1/tasks POST /v1/decide-extract POST /decide POST /extract Types Shared conventions # Input is required. Every request needs model plus exactly one of context or messages . The contract expresses this as a oneOf over those two fields. Output is batched and keyed. /v1/tasks answers every task in one response, keyed by each task's name . See structured output . Strictness. Unknown fields are rejected, not ignored. Requests that validate locally in your client will validate on the server, but requests hand-built as JSON can fail. Aliases exist for compatibility. Old names are still accepted and old names are still returned. New code should use name , results , options and keys . See versioning . Non-streaming. There is no streaming endpoint and stream is not a valid field. Shared request fields # Present on every request: Field Type Required Default model string yes - context string one of - messages array of Message one of - images array of ImageInput no - audio array of AudioInput no - temperature number, 0-2 no 0 max_output_tokens integer, 1-4096 no 16 response_format { type: "json_object" } no json_object target_language enum no - output_language enum no alias Response envelope # Field Type Notes id string Request id, for logs and support model string The model that ran choices array, exactly one OpenAI-shaped copy of the answer results object The canonical answers, keyed by task name tasks object Alias of results usage Usage Token counts Status codes # Status Meaning 200 Success 400 Malformed request, or missing context / messages 401 Missing or invalid API key 403 Key cannot use this model 422 Invalid values 429 Rate limited 500 Server error Every error body has the shape { "error": { "type", "message", "param?", "code?" } } . See errors .

title: POST /v1/tasks
description: Run any mix of decider and extractor tasks in a single request.
text: The main endpoint. Send every task you need answered over the same context in one request. http POST /v1/tasks Request # RunTasksRequest # Field Type Required Default Notes model string yes - Model identifier context string one of - Free-form text the tasks read messages array of Message one of - OpenAI-style turns images array of ImageInput no - Images to read audio array of AudioInput no - Audio to read tasks array of Task yes - At least one task temperature number, 0-2 no 0 Deterministic by default max_output_tokens integer, 1-4096 no 16 Room for the whole batch response_format object no json_object type must be json_object target_language enum no - Language for the results output_language enum no - Alias of target_language Exactly one of context and messages must be present. Task # A discriminated union on type : type Schema Required fields decide DecideTask name , question extract ExtractTask name , instruction json { "model" : "decider-extractor-v1" , "context" : "User says: renew subscription for 2 years. Previous plan expired 3 months ago." , "tasks" : [ { "type" : "decide" , "name" : "should_renew" , "question" : "Should we offer a renewal discount?" , "options" : [ "yes" , "no" ] } , { "type" : "extract" , "name" : "renew_term" , "instruction" : "Extract the renewal term in months" , "keys" : [ "months" ] } ] } Response # RunTasksResponse # Field Type Notes id string Request id model string Model that ran choices array of Choice Exactly one element results object Answers keyed by task name tasks object Alias of results usage Usage Token counts json { "id" : "req_9X2kFvTnQpR4w" , "model" : "decider-extractor-v1" , "choices" : [ { "message" : { "role" : "assistant" , "content" : "{\"should_renew\":{\"value\":\"yes\"},\"renew_term\":{\"months\":24}}" } , "finish_reason" : "stop" } ] , "results" : { "should_renew" : { "value" : "yes" } , "renew_term" : { "months" : 24 } } , "usage" : { "prompt_tokens" : 61 , "completion_tokens" : 9 , "total_tokens" : 70 } } Clients # ts await client. tasks . runTasks (request); python client.tasks.run_tasks(request) ruby client.tasks.run_tasks(request) rust client. tasks (). run_tasks (request). await ?; java client.tasks().runTasks(request); csharp await client.Tasks.RunTasksAsync(request); Errors # 400 , 422 , 429 , 500 with the standard error body. 401 and 403 for authentication and model access. See errors .

title: POST /v1/decide-extract
description: The original batched endpoint, kept as an alias of /v1/tasks.
text: http POST /v1/decide-extract This endpoint takes exactly the same request and returns exactly the same response as POST /v1/tasks . It is the original name, kept so that clients written against 0.1.0 and 0.2.0 keep working without a flag day. json { "model" : "decider-extractor-v1" , "context" : "User says: renew subscription for 2 years." , "tasks" : [ { "type" : "decide" , "name" : "should_renew" , "question" : "Should we offer a renewal discount?" , "options" : [ "yes" , "no" ] } ] } New code # Use /v1/tasks . The name says what the endpoint does, and it leaves room for task types that are neither a decision nor an extraction. diff -client.tasks.decideExtract(request); +client.tasks.runTasks(request); Behaviour # Identical to /v1/tasks : same request schema, same response schema, same validation, same errors, same token usage. The two paths are served by the same handler, so there is no behavioural difference to reason about and no feature is available on one and not the other. Deprecation # Not deprecated. It is supported for the foreseeable future, and it is the path used by the decideExtract method in every client. It will only be removed in a major version, and a major version will keep it available behind an explicit opt-out first.

title: POST /decide
description: Run one decider task without wrapping it in a list.
text: http POST /decide Use this when there is exactly one decision to make. The task fields move up to the top level and the response is flat. Request # DecideRequest # Field Type Required Default model string yes - question string yes - context string one of - messages array of Message one of - images array of ImageInput no - audio array of AudioInput no - options array of string no - choices array of string no alias of options instruction string no - temperature number, 0-2 no 0 max_output_tokens integer, 1-4096 no 16 response_format object no json_object target_language enum no - output_language enum no alias json { "model" : "decider-extractor-v1" , "context" : "User says: renew subscription for 2 years. Previous plan expired 3 months ago." , "question" : "Should we offer a renewal discount?" , "options" : [ "yes" , "no" ] } Response # DecideResponse # Field Type Notes id string Request id model string Model that ran choices array of Choice Exactly one element result DecideResult Canonical answer decision DecideResult Alias of result value string The bare answer usage Usage Token counts DecideResult # Field Type Required value string yes reason string no json { "id" : "req_4Kd8PwPq" , "model" : "decider-extractor-v1" , "choices" : [ { "message" : { "role" : "assistant" , "content" : "{\"value\":\"yes\"}" } , "finish_reason" : "stop" } ] , "result" : { "value" : "yes" , "reason" : "Two-year term and a three-month lapse" } , "decision" : { "value" : "yes" , "reason" : "Two-year term and a three-month lapse" } , "value" : "yes" , "usage" : { "prompt_tokens" : 44 , "completion_tokens" : 6 , "total_tokens" : 50 } } Clients # ts await client. tasks . decide (request); python client.tasks.decide(request) ruby client.tasks.decide(request) rust client. tasks (). decide (request). await ?; java client.tasks().decide(request); csharp await client.Tasks.DecideAsync(request); Errors # 400 without context or messages , 422 for a bad question or an out-of-range temperature or max_output_tokens , plus the standard authentication and rate-limit failures. See errors .

title: POST /extract
description: Run one extractor task without wrapping it in a list.
text: http POST /extract Use this when there is exactly one extraction to perform. Request # ExtractRequest # Field Type Required Default model string yes - instruction string yes - context string one of - messages array of Message one of - images array of ImageInput no - audio array of AudioInput no - keys array of string no - fields array of string no alias of keys schema object no JSON-Schema-like shape temperature number, 0-2 no 0 max_output_tokens integer, 1-4096 no 16 response_format object no json_object target_language enum no - output_language enum no alias json { "model" : "decider-extractor-v1" , "context" : "User says: renew subscription for 2 years. Previous plan expired 3 months ago." , "instruction" : "Extract the renewal term in months" , "keys" : [ "months" ] } Response # ExtractResponse # Field Type Notes id string Request id model string Model that ran choices array of Choice Exactly one element result object The extracted fields data object Alias of result usage Usage Token counts json { "id" : "req_7Lq2XzVb" , "model" : "decider-extractor-v1" , "choices" : [ { "message" : { "role" : "assistant" , "content" : "{\"months\":24}" } , "finish_reason" : "stop" } ] , "result" : { "months" : 24 } , "data" : { "months" : 24 } , "usage" : { "prompt_tokens" : 41 , "completion_tokens" : 5 , "total_tokens" : 46 } } result is whatever the keys or schema asked for, so it is a free-form object. With schema the shape follows that schema. Clients # ts await client. tasks . extract (request); python client.tasks.extract(request) ruby client.tasks.extract(request) rust client. tasks (). extract (request). await ?; java client.tasks().extract(request); csharp await client.Tasks.ExtractAsync(request); Errors # 400 without context or messages , 422 for an empty keys array or a malformed schema , plus the standard failures. See errors .

title: Types
description: Every schema in the contract, field by field.
text: Generated from fern/openapi/openapi.yml . When this page and the contract disagree, the contract wins and the clients follow it. Tasks # DecideTask # Field Type Required Notes type "decide" yes Discriminator name string yes Result key. ^[a-zA-Z0-9_][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]{0,63}$ question string yes The question to answer options array of string no At least one item choices array of string no Alias of options instruction string no Extra guidance target_language enum no Per-task language override id string no Legacy alias of name ExtractTask # Field Type Required Notes type "extract" yes Discriminator name string yes Result key, same pattern as DecideTask instruction string yes What to extract keys array of string no Expected field names fields array of string no Alias of keys schema object no JSON-Schema-like shape, extra properties allowed target_language enum no Per-task language override id string no Legacy alias of name Task # oneOf of DecideTask and ExtractTask , discriminated on type . Content # Message # Field Type Required Notes role enum yes system , user , assistant content string or array of ContentPart yes language enum no Language of the message ContentPart # Field Type Notes type enum text , image_url , image , audio , input_audio text string When type is text language enum Language of this part image_url ImageUrl When type is image_url image ImageInput When type is image audio AudioInput When type is audio input_audio AudioInput When type is input_audio ImageUrl # Field Type Required Default url string yes - detail enum no auto . One of low , high , auto ImageInput # Field Type Notes type enum url or base64 url string When type is url data string Base64 payload, when type is base64 mime_type string image/png , image/jpeg , image/webp , image/gif AudioInput # Field Type Notes type enum url or base64 url string When type is url data string Base64 payload, when type is base64 mime_type string audio/mp3 , audio/wav , audio/mpeg , audio/ogg , audio/mp4 Responses # Choice # Field Type Required Notes message ResponseMessage yes finish_reason enum yes stop , length , content_filter . Defaults to stop ResponseMessage # Field Type Required Notes role "assistant" yes content string yes The answers as a JSON string language enum no Language of the answer DecideResult # Field Type Required value string yes reason string no Usage # Field Type Required prompt_tokens integer >= 0 yes completion_tokens integer >= 0 yes total_tokens integer >= 0 yes Errors # ErrorResponse # Field Type Required error object yes Error object # Field Type Required Notes type string yes Broad category message string yes Safe to log param string no Offending field code string no Stable machine-readable code Language enum # Used by target_language , output_language , Message.language , ContentPart.language and ResponseMessage.language : en , es , fr , de , it , pt , nl , ru , ja , ko , zh , ar , hi , tr , pl , sv , da , no , fi , cs

title: Repository
description: How this SDK repository is laid out, and what each part is for.
headings: The contract is the source of truth#
text: The SDKs are generated from one contract. Nothing in packages/ is written by hand. text fern/ fern.config.json Fern project config, pins the CLI version generators.yml which generators run, at which versions, writing where openapi/openapi.yml THE CONTRACT, including the released version packages/ sdk-ts/ generated TypeScript client -> npm sdk-py/ generated Python client -> PyPI sdk-ruby/ generated Ruby client -> release asset sdk-rust/ generated Rust client -> release asset sdk-java/ generated Java client -> release asset sdk-csharp/ generated .NET client -> release asset scripts/ generate.mjs regenerate every SDK at the contract version bump.mjs bump the version and regenerate test.mjs build and test whichever SDKs exist prepublish-check.mjs everything that must hold before a release build-artifacts.mjs build every package, collect files for the release build-docs.mjs docs/*.md -> sites/ check-docs.mjs link and front matter checks docs/ the documentation you are reading sites/ generated site, gitignored, pushed to the sites branch release-artifacts/ generated files attached to the GitHub Release The contract is the source of truth # fern/openapi/openapi.yml defines the endpoints, the schemas and info.version . Everything else is derived: the clients, the docs' type reference, the version stamped into every package. info.version is the only version in the repository. npm, PyPI, the git tag, the GitHub Release and every attached artifact carry that number. Generated code is committed # packages/ is committed so the clients are browsable, greppable and diffable in review. The cost is that it can go stale, which CI prevents: the Generate SDKs job regenerates from the contract and fails if the result differs from what is committed, or if nothing was committed. If you do not have Docker locally, push the contract change and the Regenerate SDKs workflow opens a chore: regenerate SDKs pull request for you. Merge it and CI goes green. Contract changes and packages/ changes belong in the same commit, which is exactly what that pull request does. Local commands # Command What it does npm run fern:check Validate the contract and generator config npm run fern:generate Regenerate every SDK. Needs Docker npm run fern:check:drift Regenerate and fail if the committed SDKs are stale npm run version:print Print the contract version npm run version:bump -- patch Bump the version and regenerate npm test Build and test every generated SDK npm run release:check The full pre-publish gate npm run build:artifacts Build every package and collect release files npm run docs:build Build the docs site into sites/ npm run docs:serve Preview the docs site locally Upgrading # bash npm run fern:upgrade # the Fern CLI cd fern && fern generator upgrade --generator fern-typescript-sdk --list cd fern && fern generator upgrade --generator fern-python-sdk --list Then regenerate, test and commit. Generator bumps are ordinary dependency updates. See also # Developing the SDKs Publishing Deploying the docs

title: C++ and other clients
description: Using the API from C++, and from anything else without a generated client.
text: Fern has no C++ generator, so there is no sdk-cpp . The API is plain JSON over HTTP, so any HTTP library works and the example below is complete. C++ with cpr and nlohmann/json # cpp # include <cpr/cpr.h> # include <nlohmann/json.hpp> # include <iostream> using json = nlohmann::json; json decide_extract ( const std::string& base_url, const std::string& token, const json& request) { auto response = cpr:: Post ( cpr::Url{base_url + "/v1/tasks" }, cpr::Header{{ "Authorization" , "Bearer " + token}}, cpr::Body{request. dump ()} ); if (response.status_code != 200 ) { throw std:: runtime_error ( "decide-extractor: " + std:: to_string (response.status_code) + " " + response.text); } return json:: parse (response.text); } int main () { json request = { { "model" , "decider-extractor-v1" }, { "context" , "User says: renew subscription for 2 years." }, { "tasks" , json:: array ({ { { "type" , "decide" }, { "name" , "should_renew" }, { "question" , "Should we offer a renewal discount?" }, { "options" , json:: array ({ "yes" , "no" })} }, { { "type" , "extract" }, { "name" , "renew_term" }, { "instruction" , "Extract the renewal term in months" }, { "keys" , json:: array ({ "months" })} } })} }; auto response = decide_extract ( "http://localhost:8080" , std:: getenv ( "DEXA_TOKEN" ), request); if (response. contains ( "results" )) { std::cout << response[ "results" ]. dump ( 2 ) << "\n" ; } } bash # vcpkg.json { "dependencies" : [ "cpr" , "nlohmann-json" ] } cmake -B build && cmake --build build ./build/decide_extract The same shape works with libcurl, Boost.Beast or any other HTTP client, and with any JSON library. Only two things matter: send Authorization: Bearer <token> and read the answers from results . Generating your own client # If your language has an OpenAPI generator, point it at the published contract: bash curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dsainvg/dexa-ai-sdk/main/fern/openapi/openapi.yml bash openapi-generator generate -i openapi.yml -g cpp-httplib -o ./client bash openapi-generator generate -i openapi.yml -g typescript-fetch -o ./client bash openapi-generator generate -i openapi.yml -g python -o ./client Treat the output as you would treat the Fern clients: generated, regenerable, never edited. The contract is the interface # Whatever language you use, the contract in fern/openapi/openapi.yml is what you code against. If your generator cannot produce something sensible from it, that is a contract problem worth fixing in the OpenAPI rather than working around in every client.

title: Publishing
description: What goes to a registry, what is attached to the release, and how a release runs.
headings: Publishing the other four to real registries later#
text: Releases are driven by git tags. Push a v* tag and the release workflow verifies the repo, publishes to npm, PyPI, RubyGems and crates.io, attaches every language to the GitHub Release, and opens the release itself. Four secrets: NPM_TOKEN , PYPI_API_TOKEN , RUBY_API_KEY and CRATES_API_KEY . The docs site is published from the sites branch with the automatic GITHUB_TOKEN , so no Cloudflare credentials live in this repository. Where each package goes # Package Destination TypeScript npm, published as @dsainvg/dexa-ai-sdk Python PyPI, published as dexa-ai-sdk Ruby RubyGems, published as dexa-ai-sdk Rust crates.io, published as dexa-ai-sdk Java GitHub Release asset, com.dsainvg:dexa-ai-sdk .NET GitHub Release asset, DexaAiSdk C++ none, call the HTTP API directly The release also carries one archive per language, so a download exists for every language whether or not it has a registry. Installing the release-asset packages # bash npm install @dsainvg/dexa-ai-sdk pip install dexa-ai-sdk gem install dexa-ai-sdk cargo add dexa-ai-sdk dotnet add package -- source https://github.com/dsainvg/decide-extract-sdk/releases/download/v0.5.0 DexaAiSdk.0.5.0.nupkg Maven has no equivalent one-liner. Point your build at the release download, or add it as an artifact repository and depend on com.dsainvg:dexa-ai-sdk . What each branch is for # Branch Written by Holds main you the contract, the generated SDKs, the workflows generated/sdks Regenerate SDKs freshly generated SDKs waiting to be merged diagnostics/java-build CI the Java build log, because a failed job's log cannot be read otherwise sites nothing writes to it any more the last site published by the old branch deployer The docs site is published by the Docs workflow itself, with ctions/configure-pages, ctions/upload-pages-artifact and ctions/deploy-pages. The gate # Before anything is published or attached, one job runs every check that must hold: bash npm run release:check the contract exists and parses the tag matches info.version fern check passes regenerating produces no drift every generated package carries the contract version every generated package builds and produces its distributable artifact the npm and PyPI credentials are present If any of it fails, nothing is published and nothing is attached. Cutting a release # bash npm run version:bump -- minor git add fern/openapi/openapi.yml packages git commit -m "release: v0.4.0" git tag -a v0.4.0 -m "v0.4.0" git push origin main --tags The bump script edits the contract, regenerates and prints these commands. If regeneration fails because Docker is not running, run it again once Docker is up and commit both changes together. What the workflow does # Job Does verify Compares the tag with info.version gate Runs the full pre-publish check npm install, build, publish with provenance pypi build, publish by token or trusted publishing artifacts builds every package and collects the files github-release attaches the files and creates the release with generated notes The release is created only after the publishes succeed, so the download list on a release always matches what is actually on npm and PyPI. Publishing the other four to real registries later # It is a small change: add a publish job, its secret, and a registry entry in scripts/prepublish-check.mjs . Until then the release assets are the distribution channel, and nothing is lost by switching later, since the same version can be uploaded to a registry without republishing to npm or PyPI. Troubleshooting # The gate says a package version does not match the contract. The generated code is from an older contract. Run npm run fern:generate and commit. A publish job was skipped. Its secret is not set. Only npm and PyPI can be skipped this way. An artifact job failed. Usually a toolchain issue: cargo package needs description and license in Cargo.toml , dotnet pack needs a non-empty PackageId . Set them in fern/generators.yml so the fix survives regeneration.

title: Developing the SDKs
description: Changing the API, regenerating, and keeping CI green.
text: Changing the API # Edit fern/openapi/openapi.yml . npm run fern:check to validate it. npm run fern:generate to regenerate every client. Needs Docker. npm test to build and test them. Commit the contract and packages/ together. CI regenerates from scratch and fails if the committed output differs, so step 3 is not optional. Adding an endpoint # Give it an operationId . It becomes the method name in every client. Give it a summary . It becomes the docstring and JSDoc comment. Tag it, so it lands in the right subclient. Use oneOf with a discriminator for polymorphic payloads, the way Task does. Making a change safely # Adding an optional field is a minor version. Existing requests stay valid, and clients gain the field. Renaming a field is a major version. Add the new name, keep the old one as an alias for a full minor release, then remove it in the next major. id to name , and tasks to results , were done exactly this way. Adding an endpoint is a minor version. Tightening validation is a major version. Rejecting a request that used to succeed breaks callers who never find out until they deploy. Keeping the docs in step # The reference pages are written by hand, so they can drift from the contract. Two checks keep that visible: npm run docs:build fails if docs.config.json says a different version than the contract. node scripts/check-docs.mjs fails on broken internal links and on pages missing a title or description. If you add a field, update the type reference and the relevant guide in the same commit. What CI runs # Job Checks Contract fern check Generate SDKs regenerates, then fails on drift TypeScript , Python , Ruby , Rust , Java , .NET build and test each client Docs site builds the site, checks links Regenerate SDKs opens a pull request when packages/ is missing or stale Release the full pre-publish gate, then publishes and attaches artifacts Without Docker # npm run fern:generate needs Docker because Fern runs each generator in a container. If you cannot run it locally, push the contract change: the Regenerate SDKs workflow does it on a runner and opens a chore: regenerate SDKs pull request containing packages/ . Merge it and the drift check passes. Requirements for a local run # Tool Needed for Node 20+ everything Docker fern generate --local , which is how all six generators run Python 3.9+, uv the Python client Ruby 3.3+ the Ruby client Rust stable the Rust client JDK 17+, Maven the Java client .NET SDK 8 the .NET client Toolchains that are not installed are skipped with a message rather than failing, so you can work on just the languages you have. See also # Repository layout Publishing Deploying the docs

title: Deploying the docs
description: Building sites/ and publishing it to the sites branch.
headings: Pointing a host at the branch#
text: The documentation is markdown in docs/ . The site in sites/ is generated from it and pushed to a sites branch in this repository, which is what gets published. Only the markdown is committed to main . Build # bash npm run docs:build # docs/*.md -> sites/ npm run docs:serve # preview on http://localhost:4321 bash npm run docs:build -- --base /decide-extractor-docs/ npm run docs:serve -- --base /decide-extractor-docs/ --base matters if the site is served from a subpath rather than the root of a domain. What the build does # renders every page in docs/ that is not marked hidden: true groups pages into sections from the folder they live in adds heading anchors, a table of contents, a sidebar and previous/next links resolves .md links to real URLs and fails on broken ones highlights code blocks, styles callouts and tables emits llms.txt and llm.txt , the machine-readable summary from docs/llms-template.md with the page index appended, plus search-index.json , sitemap.xml and robots.txt llms.txt # llms.txt is the summary an assistant reads instead of crawling the site. It carries what is needed to call the API: authentication, the four endpoints, both task types with every field, the shared request fields, the response envelope, multimodal input, the language enum, the error codes and the conventions that bite. It is written by hand in docs/llms-template.md ; the build appends an index of every page. Both llms.txt and llm.txt are published, with identical content, because both names are in use. npm run docs:build && node scripts/check-docs.mjs fails if they drift apart, go missing, or lose a required section. Front matter # markdown --- title: Quickstart description: Send your first request. order: 2 --- Key Purpose title Sidebar label and page heading. Required description The one-line summary. Required, also used for meta tags order Position within the section section Override the section name, which otherwise comes from the folder hidden true keeps the page out of the site, nav and search Design notes and internal documents live in docs/ with hidden: true , so they stay in the repository without ending up on the website. Checks # bash node scripts/check-docs.mjs Fails on broken internal links, missing front matter, and a docs.config.json version that has drifted from the contract. How it is published # .github/workflows/docs.yml runs on every push to main : builds the site into sites/ runs the link and front matter checks publishes to the sites branch Pull requests only build and check. The sites branch is the only branch here that anything but a human writes to. The site is versioned # Each release keeps the documentation it shipped with: / the newest published version /v0-5-0/ 0.5.0 exactly as published /v0-3-5/ 0.3.5 exactly as published /versions.json the list the version switcher reads Publishing writes the folder for the current contract version and refreshes the root. No other version folder is touched, so rebuilding a version replaces only that version, and a new release adds a folder instead of overwriting the last one. npm run docs:publish does the same thing locally. bash git clone --branch sites --depth 1 https://github.com/dsainvg/decide-extract-sdk.git _site The push uses the automatic GITHUB_TOKEN with contents: write , so there is nothing to configure in this repository and no Cloudflare credentials to store. Pointing a host at the branch # Any static host that can build from a git branch works. Create the project once, then set it to watch sites rather than main . For a Cloudflare Pages project: connect the repository, then set the production branch to sites and leave the build command empty, since the branch already contains the finished site. Cloudflare redeploys whenever the branch moves, which is every push to main . Add CNAME to docs/ if you want a custom domain: the build copies it to the site root, and the branch will carry it. See also # Repository layout Contributing to the docs

title: Naming
description: Why the generated packages are named after the organization, and how to fix it.
text: What the generators produce today # Language Package name Manifest TypeScript sources only, no package.json missing Python sources only, no pyproject.toml missing Ruby dsainvg dsainvg.gemspec Rust dexa-ai-sdk Cargo.toml Java org.dsainvg maintained in templates/sdk-java/pom.xml .NET DexaAiSdk DexaAiSdk.csproj Why # Fern derives the SDK's package identity from the API name . This project was created with bash fern init --api --org dsainvg --openapi contracts/openapi.yaml which registers the API under the organization and leaves it without a name of its own, so every generator falls back to the organization identifier. dsainvg , dexa-ai-sdk and DexaAiSdk are all that fallback. The three generators that need a package name to emit a manifest at all, TypeScript, Python and Java, fail differently as a result: they write sources and skip the manifest. The Python generator refuses to start if handed a key it does not recognise, so a wrong key such as package-name fails the generator outright, while package_name is accepted and still leaves the output without a manifest. fern.config.json cannot fix this. It accepts only organization and version ; projectId , name , apiId , api-id , project-id , project , apiName and api-name are all rejected as unrecognized keys. The fix # Give the API a name in Fern, which means signing in and creating or renaming the API in the Fern dashboard, or re-running fern init against a named API: bash fern login fern init --api --org dsainvg --openapi fern/openapi/openapi.yml Once the API is named, set the package name for each generator in fern/generators.yml and regenerate. The manifests and the names follow from the contract's info.title , Dexa API . What this does not affect # The API surface itself. Endpoints, schemas and request and response shapes come from the contract and are correct in every generated client. The TypeScript, Python and Java clients as source. The generated code is complete and correct; only the packaging metadata is missing, which is what makes them unbuildable and unpublishable. Ruby, Rust and .NET, which build and test today under their organization-derived names. Working around it # The three clients are still published and usable. Their package manifests are maintained here rather than in packages/ , because Fern wipes each output directory before it generates, so anything written inside packages/ by hand is deleted on the next run. The manifests live in templates/sdk-ts/ and templates/sdk-py/ , with __VERSION__ where the version goes, and scripts/write-manifests.mjs renders them into packages/ after generation with info.version from the contract. npm run fern:generate calls it automatically, so the manifests can never drift from the contract version. File Purpose templates/sdk-ts/package.json npm package: name, version, exports, build scripts templates/sdk-ts/tsconfig.json compiler options for the generated sources templates/sdk-ts/tsconfig.build.json build config emitting dist/ with declarations templates/sdk-py/pyproject.toml PyPI package: name, version, dependencies, packaging Because Python's generated tree is flat, pyproject.toml maps the whole directory to one package and lists each subpackage, otherwise setuptools builds a wheel with only the top-level modules. The import name is dexa_ai_sdk , which is what the generator's own docstrings, User-Agent header and tests reference. The Ruby gem needs no equivalent: Fern generates custom.gemspec.rb as a documented hook for exactly this, so the gem's name and metadata are set there and protected with .fernignore . Do not add .fernignore to packages/sdk-ts or packages/sdk-py : Fern runs git reset -- on the ignored paths with NUL-separated arguments, which fails on Linux runners with ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE .
